topics.label: Introduction and Lecture Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class and outlines the learning goals for the final lecture on cancer therapy.

topics.label: Conventional Cancer Therapies: Surgery, Radiotherapy, and Cytotoxic Chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the principles, clinical successes, and toxic limitations of standard cancer treatments.

topics.label: Exploiting Cancer Cell Vulnerabilities and Checkpoint Defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore therapeutic strategies that target intrinsic vulnerabilities of cancer cells, including hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint loss, and defective DNA repair.

topics.label: Oncogene Addiction, Kinase Inhibitors, and Mechanisms of Resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the development of targeted therapies against hyperactive oncogenic kinases and the mechanisms by which tumors evolve drug resistance and addiction.

topics.label: Therapeutic Monoclonal Antibodies and Antibody-Drug Conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how engineered antibodies are used to block cell surface receptors, recruit immune effector mechanisms, or deliver cytotoxic payloads directly to tumor cells.

topics.label: Cancer Immunotherapy and T-Cell Engagement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on harnessing and enhancing host T-cell immunity against cancer via immune checkpoint inhibitors, bispecific T-cell engagers, and CAR T cells.

topics.label: Challenges, Progress, and Future Directions in Cancer Therapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics reflect on historical survival trends, ongoing hurdles such as tumor heterogeneity, and future clinical and ethical perspectives in cancer management.
